what: Unum sells employee benefits: disability insurance that pays part of someone's salary if they cannot work, group life, dental and supplemental health cover, mostly bought by employers for their staff.
customers: Employers in the United States and Britain, who offer the cover to employees.
money: group disability, life and supplemental benefits
the same products in Britain and Poland
voluntary benefits sold at the workplace
the long-term care policies no longer sold
moat: Relationships with employers and the claims data of a century of disability underwriting, which is what lets it price a risk most insurers avoid.
risks: The closed long-term care block still requires reserve strengthening from time to time
52 times earnings because a reserve charge depressed the latest year's profit
Disability claims rise in a recession, exactly when premiums stop growing
opportunities: 7.3 times free cash flow with $1.6B of free cash flow against a $11.9B market value
Analysts see about 26% upside, with 13 covering the stock
Higher bond yields raise investment income on the reserves backing long-dated policies
watch: Benefit ratios in group disability and any further long-term care reserve action.
